title: Multi-Horizon Metric Curation and Trace Annotation Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a pragmatic process for curating observability signals across three operational horizons and a compact standard for trace annotations for tokenized inference flows. Goal: keep dashboards and traces actionable for oncall, product, and capacity planning while controlling cardinality and query cost.

Scope:
- Applies to inference control plane, model serving runtime, and routing/fallback layers.
- Covers metric selection, retention/aggregation guidance, trace annotation keys, dashboard composition templates, and rollout checklist.

High-level idea — three horizons:
- Horizon 0 (Triage): signals SREs need to detect / escalate incidents within 0–15m. Low-cardinality, high-frequency, 1m granularity. Examples: request_rate, error_rate_5xx, p50_token_latency, kv_cache_hit_rate (global), reserved_capacity_utilization.
- Horizon 1 (Health + Feature Ops): signals product/ops use to validate rollouts and QoS over days. Medium-cardinality, 1h granularity. Examples: per-route latency quantiles, model_variant_quality_regressions (aggregate by experiment), tail_kv_miss_fraction_by_model.
- Horizon 2 (Capacity & Cost): signals for capacity planning and model economics. Low-sample rate, daily/weekly windows. Examples: tokens_per_customer_per_day, avg_tokens_per_completion_by_model_family, cost_per_k_token_estimate.

Metric curation rules (practical):
- One source of truth metric name per concept (avoid duplicates). Namespace: inference.<layer>.<concept> (e.g., inference.runtime.token_latency_ms).
- Cardinality cap: prefer <=3 dynamic tags (model, tenant_bucket, route); anything more requires an approval and aggregation plan.
- Aggregation tiers: raw 1m -> rollups 5m/1h/1d. Store high-res for 30d, rollups for 90d, coarse for 365d.
- Cost tag policy: only include tenant_id for triage when tied to incidents; use tenant_bucket for dashboards.
- Alerting: alerts defined on horizon-0 representations (p95/p99 depending on incident class) with annotations linking to traces and runbooks.

Trace annotation standard (compact key set):
Include a small, consistent set of top-level attributes on every server-side root span for inference requests. Keys must be short, stable, and human-friendly. Recommended keys: 
- session_id 
- request_id 
- route_name 
- model_version 
- model_family 
- batch_size (int)
- kv_cache_hit (true|false)
- quant_profile (enum)
- fallback_reason (if any)
- prompt_hash (short)
- duration_ms
- tenant_bucket

Annotation guidelines:
- Avoid logging full prompt text in traces (PII & cost). Use prompt_hash and storage pointer if replay needed.
- Use boolean flags for cache hits, fallback, and routing fallthroughs to make filtering cheap.
- Prefer short enums for quant_profile and fallback_reason to avoid high-cardinality strings.

Dashboard composition: templates and priorities
- Triage board (single panel row): global QPS, errors, p50/p95 token latency, largest recent error traces (linked), active rollout flag. Keep to 6–8 panels.
- Route health board: per-route rate, latency heatmap, kv_cache_warmth_index, recent degraded model variants. Use embedded quick-links to trace queries pre-populated with route+time filters.
- Economy board: tokens/day, cost-estimate by model_family, batch_efficiency (tokens_per_gpu_hour), reserved_vs_burst_utilization. Add churn indicators for model upgrades.

Investigation affordances (practical widgets):
- Pre-built trace link that injects last 1h filter and session_id bucket.
- Prompt-replay sampler: store sampled prompts in an audit bucket and expose pointer in trace. Sampling budget limited to 0.1% by default.
- KV cache warmth index: heuristic combining recent warm fraction and miss spikes; surface when it drops >10% relative to baseline.

Rollout instrumentation checklist (before/after a canary):
- Add canary tag on requests and model_variant tag on metrics.
- Ensure traces include fallback_reason and prompt_hash.
- Add a lightweight synthetic probe that exercises the critical route at 1m cadence with known prompts.
- Monitor Horizon-0 SLI drift for 2h post-rollout.

Migration and pruning plan:
- Quarterly curation sweep: remove metrics with query < 10/mo and no linked runbook.
- Rename policy: new metric name allowed for breaking changes only; keep legacy alias for 30d with redirect.

Open questions / decisions to escalate:
- Retention sizing for raw token-level histograms — propose keeping 7d raw then rolling to TDigest for 90d.
- Default sampling rate for prompt-replay — currently propose 0.1% but product may request higher for quality monitoring.

Action items (owners):
- (Avery) Draft migration runbook and alias mapping by 2024-11-20.
- (Marcus) Implement tracer attribute enum set and add to instrumentation linting by 2024-12-05.
- (Elena) Create dashboard skeletons and probe jobs by 2024-12-15.

Notes to reviewers:
- This playbook is intentionally opinionated: pick a small set of high-value signals and keep traces lean. We can expand horizon definitions after two pilot rollouts.

Appendix — example metric names (suggested):
- inference.runtime.request_rate_by_route
- inference.runtime.token_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99
- inference.runtime.kv_cache_hit_rate
- inference.routing.fallback_rate_by_model_variant
- inference.economy.tokens_per_customer_1d

End of doc.
